title: Three kinds of evidence answer different questions
caption: Dimensional measurement, defect inspection and electrical behavior are complementary. Passing one does not establish all the others.

nodes.label: Metrology
nodes.detail: How thick, wide or well aligned is the intended structure?

nodes.label: Inspection
nodes.detail: Is an unexpected particle, bridge or missing feature present?

nodes.label: Electrical test
nodes.detail: Does the structure behave as the test requires?

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Inspect broadly, then investigate selectively
caption: Detailed images cover limited area at a time. Sampling and review strategies balance sensitivity, throughput and the cost of missed defects.

nodes.label: Broad inspection
nodes.detail: Survey the wafer for suspicious features.

nodes.label: Selected sites
nodes.detail: Choose locations using signals and a sampling plan.

nodes.label: Detailed review
nodes.detail: Examine a smaller region at higher resolution.

nodes.label: Process decision
nodes.detail: Use the evidence to investigate, hold or continue.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Yield is defined at a particular stage
caption: Each test or assembly stage has its own acceptance requirements. A useful yield number identifies both the unit and the criterion.

nodes.label: Processed wafer
nodes.detail: Early process checks assess wafer-level conditions.

nodes.label: Die sort
nodes.detail: Electrical tests classify individual dies.

nodes.label: Assembly
nodes.detail: Suitable dies become a package with new interfaces.

nodes.label: Product bins
nodes.detail: Final requirements determine useful grades or rejection.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Temporary contacts connect each die to the tester
caption: A prober positions the wafer, the probe card supplies contacts and ATE exercises the selected die. The resulting wafer map guides later selection.

nodes.label: Wafer and prober
nodes.detail: Place each die at the required contact position.

nodes.label: Probe card
nodes.detail: Make temporary electrical connections.

nodes.label: ATE
nodes.detail: Apply stimuli and evaluate measured responses.

nodes.label: Wafer map
nodes.detail: Record pass, fail and product-bin information.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Assembly creates new things to test
caption: Known-good die means a specified incoming test flow passed. Package connections, stresses and system interfaces require additional evidence.

nodes.label: Screened die
nodes.detail: Passes its incoming test requirements.

nodes.label: Assembly
nodes.detail: Creates joints and combines materials or dies.

nodes.label: Package test
nodes.detail: Exercises newly formed electrical interfaces.

nodes.label: Reliability evidence
nodes.detail: Evaluates behavior under specified stresses and conditions.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Choose test coverage around the consequences
caption: Testing consumes time and resources, while escapes put downstream value at risk. The decision must reflect the failure mechanism and product context.

nodes.label: Possible failure
nodes.detail: Identify what could escape the current flow.

nodes.label: Downstream exposure
nodes.detail: Consider valuable neighbors and wasted system time.

nodes.label: Test cost
nodes.detail: Account for equipment time and usable device lifetime.

nodes.label: Coverage decision
nodes.detail: Choose evidence proportionate to the stated risks.
